canonical_data: a vault of Markdown notes on disk, named by hierarchy, with schemas and configuration the user owns
current_repo_note: Archived on the maintainer's own published declaration, not on a platform flag: the readme states active development has ceased and the project is in maintenance only, following a public announcement that the company behind it did not find a viable business. No successor is named, so the supersession status does not apply. The last commit touching product code is from August 2023, no releases exist, and the editor extension has not been updated since; its documentation site and published vaults still resolve. A search across its whole source tree finds no model or embedding code, so it is a plain note tool rather than an assisted one.
strengths: Hierarchical naming with schemas makes structure enforceable rather than conventional, so a large vault stays navigable by lookup instead of by memory
Notes are ordinary Markdown files on disk that survive the tool, and the publishing pipeline turns a vault into a site the author owns
Import and export adapters move whole vaults between other note tools without a proprietary intermediate format
weaknesses: Development ceased in early 2023 by the maintainer's own declaration, with no release since and hundreds of issues left open
It has no model or embedding code anywhere in its tree, so every assisted-retrieval capability its neighbours offer is absent
Licence metadata is inconsistent: several packages declare no licence at all, others use a non-standard identifier string, and a notice file asserts all rights reserved beside a permissive licence
why_it_matters: The most complete worked example of hierarchy and schemas as the organising principle of a note vault, and a reminder that a widely installed tool can stop without its files becoming unreadable.
